title: Canonical metric spec (D3b output)
description: THE canonical, vendor-neutral metric artifact. One writer (x3_emit, the card gate), many readers: every output plug projects from this and never from another plug's output, and none computes a field that is not here. A superset by design — each target takes its slice; an unused field is correct, a derived one is not.

spec_version.description: The card contract version. Explicit dispatch: a reader performs no implicit upgrade or downgrade.

partial.description: Present only when X3 ran with --partial and some merged metrics have no card. The layer is NOT publishable: r1b and g1 refuse it. Lists the merged metrics still unauthored.

metric_refs_by_vq.description: Inverted `derived_from`: which metrics each verified query computes. R1 publishes it on every record, and it is what makes the metric layer and the verified-query layer checkable against each other (§4.4).

metric_ref.description: Family-scoped reference used to join slices and examples back to this metric.

source_id.description: The stable identity, derived from the MEASURE, not from the grouping. Renaming, regrouping and reformatting must not move it — an identity that shifts archives artifacts and REPLACES a layer that should have been REVISED.

formula.description: THE MEASURE, as SQL. The complete aggregate, fully qualified — `COUNT(DISTINCT DB.SCHEMA.T.ID)`, or the whole guarded divide for a ratio. Opaque formula text to a destination (never parsed or executed there), and it is what a consumer assembles a statement from. Prose belongs in `description` and `population`: a sentence here is a metric whose definition cannot be built.

sql.description: The canonical statement, NARROWED FROM a parent query rather than authored.

grain.description: THE KEY: the column(s) that make one row of the base table unique, comma-separated and fully qualified. It is what tells a consumer whether a join has multiplied rows. A description of the OUTPUT grain says nothing about that and belongs in `population`.

population.description: Prose and the declared filter list are derived from ONE source, so the two cannot disagree: a restriction that is not declared is not described either.

mandatory_filters.description: NOT the same list as definitional_filters: a definitional filter has a drop-when.

parameters.description: One entry per distinct NAME, values merged. Duplicate parameter names are refused outright.

zero_denominator.description: Absence and explicit null are preserved separately; a ratio with neither is flagged.

unit.description: Named only where the words say so.

sql.description: The ON condition. Opaque; never parsed.

joins.description: DECLARED, never dropped. An unresolved sub-field is admitted in place as `unknown`.

required_join.description: The join this dimension reads through, by name. A hint for readers: a consumer resolves what a dimension needs from the references in its expression and by following ON conditions, so a two-hop or two-join dimension needs nothing extra here.

dimensions.description: Column-level, in any of the five roles. Under §3.9 these carry the load `variants[]` used to — a `filtered` dimension holds every value the family observed.

dimension_report.description: What D3 could and could not resolve. Without it, a consumer reads the absence as 'every dimension resolved'.

tier.description: The trust tier, from the lane of the closure ACTUALLY PUBLISHED — not the winner's, since D3b falls back to the richest closure when the winner's was withheld and the two then differ (§3.3). Named by provenance, never by correctness, and a separate axis from the witness label: `bi_declared` + `parse_only` is a coherent state.

status.description: ALWAYS empty. A witness is not an approval; the producer never sets governance status and never sets `approved`.

derived_from.description: Every verified query computing this measure, winner first.

examples.description: The retained slices, ranked by popularity then recency and cut at `metrics.examples.retain_n`. NOTE: not structurally deduplicated — `collapse_variants` runs on records only, so two examples may be two tellings of one recipe (deferred).

group_by.description: Must name declared dimensions: an example whose group_by references an absent one is REFUSED.

result.description: Unattested producer evidence. Row width must match the declared columns, or the example is refused.

gotchas.description: What a reader has to know before trusting the number, taken from the statements this metric was mined from.

filters.description: Technical filters the statements applied but which are not definitional — column, operator, value, fully qualified. A caller may drop one and still have the same metric over a wider population.

depends_on.description: Other metrics this one is computed from.

notes.description: What the source statements disagree about, said rather than papered over.

related.description: Relations the edge vocabulary has no type for — a grain variant or an alternative. Carried on the card, never invented as an edge.

dialect.description: The warehouse this card's SQL is written for. No default: a function like DIV0NULL or a clause like QUALIFY exists in some engines only, and a card that does not say where it runs is a syntax error waiting for the first person to run it elsewhere.

source.description: The spec's source object. `sql` IS THE FROM CLAUSE: a source is a table or a SQL source, exactly one of `table` and `sql`, so this is the text after FROM. A join's INNER or LEFT is written out here, because it is the only place the contract has for it; a measure computed in two passes is derived tables joined together. Tables are never aliased here: the card's expressions are fully qualified and an alias makes them unresolvable.

synonyms.description: The model's own other names for this metric (a declared metric's synonyms, and the author's name when the card took the model's), verbatim. Retrieval words for search and the glossary; not a registry field.

viewer_binds.description: The metric is FILTERED TO THE VIEWING USER: a statement it is derived from reads the name (or full name) of whoever runs it as a bind placeholder (the union over its sources). Never the name itself (guardrail 8). `bindable`: every such source was verified bound to the fetching identity, in memory.

quality.description: The metric's conversion-quality grade: the worst grade of the BI statements it was merged from (policy `quality.order`), the reason that statement gives, and each statement's grade. Absent on a metric of the query-history lane only.

bi_definitions.description: Every BI definition this metric was merged from, one per (model, measure): where it is defined and how (its style), the model's own metadata about it (description, display folder, annotations, perspectives, the model's or data source's endorsement, a KPI's target and status) and the statements compiled from it. CONTEXT, NEVER SEMANTICS: none of it changed the SQL. Absent on a metric with no BI source.

style.description: How the BI tool defines it: `explicit` (a measure of the model), `implicit` (a column aggregated where it is used), `report` (a report's own measure over a shared model), `calculation_item` (a calculation group's item applied to the measure by the widget: `calculation_items`), `kpi_target` / `kpi_status` (a KPI's target or status expression).

derived_from.description: The other measures this one's formula names (a measure chain), by name.

calculation_items.description: The calculation group items the statement applies to the measure (`stacked`: the statement shows several, one per row), each with its formula in the model's own words.

withheld_binds.description: The statement COMPARES WITH A WITHHELD LITERAL: a person's address or name the BI file holds, which no artifact keeps (guardrail 8). It reads each one as a bind placeholder (`of` withheld_N, the same N for the same value across the run); whoever runs it binds it to the value the BI file's own formula or filter holds. Verification binds it in memory, from the BI file, and drops it.

bi_tags.description: The BI tool's own metadata about a definition, verbatim (bi_facts `tags`, plus its model's endorsement). Hints for whoever reads or authors; never used to change SQL.

labels.description: The BI tool's own tags on the model's or data source's assets (content tags).
